items.title:
eu.ciechanowiec:airness-maven-plugin 1.0.6 发布, The Maven goals that bind governance checks and explicit repair operations to the build. A check
        reads the tree without changing it unless a repair switch is set for it, and no switch is set by
        an ordinary build. The assets-sync goal writes only when called directly, and source-formatting
        writes only under the format profile.

        A check that shipped as a test could be accidentally deselected by -Dtest=OneClass. As goals the
        checks stay bound to their phases, their parameters are named and typed, and a failure names the
        check in the line that reports it. Every goal honors -DskipTests as the quality and governance
        bypass, except the publication checks, which a release must answer even though it skips the tests
        it already ran.

eu.ciechanowiec:airness-annotations 1.0.6 发布, The annotation the rule set expects to find in a consumer's source. This is the only Airness
        artifact that reaches a consuming project's compile classpath, which is why it is an artifact of
        its own rather than a package inside airness-config: folding it in would put the analyzer
        configurations on that classpath as well, to no purpose.

        It carries no dependencies and no runtime cost. The annotation has SOURCE retention, so it does
        not survive compilation into the consumer's artifact.

items.title:
eu.ciechanowiec:airness-assets 1.0.6 发布, The files the harness owns but cannot supply from a classpath, and the manifest saying what a
        project may do with each.

        Most of the harness reaches a project as configuration an analyzer reads off its own plugin
        classpath, which is why most of it needs no file in the project at all. What lands here is what
        something outside Maven reads from disk: an editor reading .editorconfig, git reading
        .gitattributes. Those have nowhere else to live, so they live in the project and are checked
        against the bytes shipped here.

        Each canonical file is stored under an added .asset suffix. A stored .gitignore under its own
        name would be a working .gitignore over this directory and could stop its neighbours from being
        tracked, and a stored .gitattributes would take effect over them. A file that changes the meaning
        of the directory it sits in cannot be stored under its own name.

net.sourceforge.pmd:pmd-visualforce 7.27.0 发布, PMD is an extensible multilanguage static code analyzer. It finds common programming flaws like unused variables,
        empty catch blocks, unnecessary object creation, and so forth. It's mainly concerned with Java and
        Apex, but supports 16 other languages. It comes with 400+ built-in rules. It can be
        extended with custom rules. It uses JavaCC and Antlr to parse source files into abstract syntax trees
        (AST) and runs rules against them to find violations. Rules can be written in Java or using a XPath query.

        Currently, PMD supports Java, JavaScript, Salesforce.com Apex and Visualforce,
        Kotlin, Swift, Modelica, PL/SQL, Apache Velocity, JSP, WSDL, Maven POM, HTML, XML and XSL.
        Scala is supported, but there are currently no Scala rules available.

        Additionally, it includes CPD, the copy-paste-detector. CPD finds duplicated code in
        Coco, C/C++, C#, CSS, Dart, Fortran, Gherkin, Go, Groovy, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSP, Julia, Kotlin,
        Lua, Matlab, Modelica, Objective-C, Perl, PHP, PL/SQL, Python, Ruby, Rust, Salesforce.com Apex and
        Visualforce, Scala, Swift, T-SQL, Typescript, Apache Velocity, WSDL, XML and XSL.
